subject.title: fix(doctor): surface multi-account default routing warnings in preview and lint

question: Should `openclaw doctor --lint` fail by default for multi-account channel configs that lack explicit default routing, or should this new `core/doctor/default-account-routing` check be opt-in or softer first?
rationale: The implementation is a reasonable diagnostics fix, but root policy treats stricter validation and fallback/default behavior as compatibility-sensitive because existing operator configs may start failing lint on upgrade.

options.title: Accept default lint warning
options.body: Merge with explicit maintainer sign-off that these warning findings should be part of default `doctor --lint` and may produce a nonzero lint exit for existing configs.

options.title: Soften lint rollout
options.body: Keep preview and repair warnings but make the structured lint check default-disabled, info-only, or otherwise opt-in until operators have migration guidance.

options.title: Defer to routing RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and decide the diagnostic/fallback policy together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97655.

recommendation.title: Accept default lint warning
recommendation.body: Merge with explicit maintainer sign-off that these warning findings should be part of default `doctor --lint` and may produce a nonzero lint exit for existing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current warning helper and repair helper lines are blamed to current-main commit f8016c44 authored by steipete, and the decision is about the same doctor/config compatibility surface.
